clue.text: Private aspiration of newly-ordained priest

indicators.note: newly ordained means set in a fresh order, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A young priest, freshly ordained, quietly hopes for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective meaning secret, but it is the army rank: a private soldier hopes for promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A private soldier's first promotion to lance corporal is marked by a chevron sewn on the sleeve, so that is what he aspires to.

clue.text: Dump old car after argument

indicators.note: after places the first-mentioned piece behind the one named next

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or quarrel
a heap is slang for a decrepit car

explanation.surface: Dumping a battered car once a row has broken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dump' looks like a verb, to abandon the car, but it is a noun: a rubbish heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of discarded junk is a rubbish tip, the place where old items end up.

clue.text: Succeed as agent with network

indicators.note: with simply sets one piece alongside the other

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative or agent
lace is a fabric made of a net of threads

explanation.surface: Doing well as an agent thanks to good business contacts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' suggests doing well; here it means take over from someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to follow them into their role, taking their place.

clue.text: A wasteful individual — a dreadful prig of late

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Calling a recent prig a spendthrift.
explanation.definitionFit: A spendthrift who squanders money recklessly is described by this noun, also an adjective.

clue.text: University people accepting cut in scales

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it inside, so one group of letters goes within the other

parts.note: Bachelors of Arts, graduates of a university
to lance is to cut, as a boil

explanation.surface: Graduates accept a reduction in their pay scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut in scales' reads like a pay cut, but 'in' is just a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of scales is a weighing instrument, also called a balance; the plural matches.

clue.text: Humiliation for a capsized sailor the crew set about

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in a down clue the word is turned over

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: taken as written
a ship's crew are its men

explanation.surface: A sailor who overturned his boat is mocked by the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lowered in dignity or esteem is a state of degradation and shame.

clue.text: The man who makes his appearance with day's end

parts.note: and means together with

indicators.note: end points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of day

explanation.surface: A man who shows up only as evening falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for Andrew, this is a common male first name, so a particular fellow.

clue.text: Calm down and make up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to settle oneself, as in collecting one's thoughts
second meaning: to create, as music or a poem

explanation.surface: Settle down after a quarrel and be reconciled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make up' suggests reconciling after a row; it means create or form.
explanation.definitionFit: One settles oneself by regaining composure, and a writer creates a piece of music or verse.

clue.text: Divine taste, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to perceive intuitively
second meaning: taste is one example of the five bodily faculties

explanation.surface: Heavenly flavour, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective, heavenly, but is the verb to intuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit something is to feel it, and taste is one of the five faculties of perception, alongside sight and hearing.

clue.text: A housewife needing some private tuition

indicators.note: some of means only a part of the following words is used

parts.note: found straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A homemaker who needs private lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: A housewife (pronounced 'hussif') is also an old word for a small sewing case, which is the sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ornamental case for needles and thread was called a housewife, a crossword-favourite sense.

clue.text: Knock the Left in sympathy

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: Criticise the political Left while claiming to feel for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Left' suggests politics, but it is the nautical left side.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, harmonious understanding between people, a mutual fellow feeling.

clue.text: Stomach trouble — bad sign

indicators.note: something in trouble is disturbed, so the following short word is jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A stomach upset taken as an ill portent.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly region of the body, containing the digestive organs, is loosely called the stomach.

clue.text: In the main he strives to come up with something of value

definitions.text: In the main he strives to come up with something of value

parts.note: surface: a man who mostly works hard; setter's reading: 'the main' is the open sea, and he works underwater

parts.words: to come up with something of value
parts.note: surface: to produce a good idea; setter's reading: literally to rise to the surface holding a gem from an oyster

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'mostly' but means 'in the sea', a poetic sense of main.
explanation.definitionFit: This person descends into the sea to gather oysters for the gems they may contain, then surfaces with them.

clue.text: Spot an animal seldom seen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small dark mark on the skin
second meaning: a burrowing creature that lives underground

explanation.surface: Catching sight of a rare creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a verb, to see the rare animal, but it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a dark blemish on the skin and a small furry burrower that rarely surfaces.

clue.text: A stony dependant

parts.note: surface: a penniless person who relies on others, stony-broke
setter's reading: something made of rock that literally hangs down from a cave roof

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dependant' suggests someone supported by another; read literally it is something hanging down.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineral icicle formed by dripping water hangs from the ceiling of a limestone cave.

clue.text: Issues Oriental blends

parts.note: E for East, the Orient
merges means combines or blends

explanation.surface: An Eastern tea company releasing its blends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issues' reads as a noun, but it is a verb meaning comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue from somewhere is to come out of it, the verb's sense of appearing.

clue.text: Setting teeth on edge

parts.note: surface: irritating someone, as a grating noise does
setter's reading: literally cutting notches along a blade's edge, as on a saw or bread knife

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'set one's teeth on edge' means annoy; taken literally it describes making a toothed blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a row of sharp notches along a blade, like those of a saw, gives it a toothed edge.

clue.text: Beg for adjustment of rent, and scoff afterwards

indicators.note: afterwards places the second piece after the first
an adjustment changes the arrangement, so the next word's letters are reordered

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: A tenant pleads for a rent change, then mocks the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' suggests mockery; in British slang it means to wolf down food.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg is to plead earnestly, which is exactly what this verb means.

clue.text: To walk around unquestioned is much appreciated

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one word goes outside the other

parts.note: to tread is to walk
something sure is certain, beyond question

explanation.surface: Being free to stroll about unchallenged is a valued liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held dear and valued highly is cherished, prized like a precious possession.

clue.text: Little page wanting second dish of food

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for page
the latter is the second of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: A small pageboy wants another helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little page' sounds like a young servant, but 'little' means abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flat serving plate, and the food arranged on it, as in a seafood platter.

clue.text: A poem about hundreds being in conflict

indicators.note: about means around, so the poem's words wrap the other piece

parts.note: a verse is a poem
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A poem concerning centuries of warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: D is 500 in Roman numerals, that is, several hundreds.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse forces are opposing or hostile ones, set against each other.

clue.text: Plough to time

parts.note: till means up to, as in nine till five
an age is a period of time

explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link word, but it supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ploughing land prepares it for crops; the noun names that cultivation or the ploughed land itself.

clue.text: A messenger or porter enveloping mail

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap up, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale
post is the British word for mail

explanation.surface: A courier or doorman delivering the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' and 'mail' suggest a building's doorman with the post; porter is a dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek apostolos means one sent out, and each of Christ's twelve was sent to spread the gospel.

clue.text: A flier took the plunge in America

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a bird, the pigeon-like bird of peace
second meaning: the American past tense of dive

explanation.surface: A pilot who made a daring commitment in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans say a diver 'dove' where Britons say 'dived'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a cooing bird and the US form of the verb meaning plunged headfirst.

clue.text: The author  of "Maud's Dilemma?

indicators.note: a dilemma is a confused predicament, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking who wrote a novel called Maud's Dilemma.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas was the French novelist who wrote The Three Musketeers, a famous writer.

clue.text: It's wrong to decline current acknowledgements of indebtedness

parts.note: to fall is to decline
AC is alternating current
an IOU is a signed note admitting a debt

explanation.surface: A moral lesson: it is wrong to refuse to acknowledge your current debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decline' reads as refuse but means fall; 'current' reads as present but is electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fallacious rests on a false argument or mistaken belief, so it is incorrect.

clue.text: Goes round for drinks

definitions.meaning: first meaning: completes circuits of a track
second meaning: drinks with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Taking a turn to buy a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes round for drinks' suggests a pub round; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner circles a track repeatedly, and a dog or cat takes up liquid with its tongue.

clue.text: A row — it upset the queen

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A quarrel that distressed the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one level in a series of ranks of seats, such as in a stadium.

clue.text: A man will take a single cocktail

parts.note: a man's first name
I is one, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A man orders one drink at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin-and-vermouth mix, garnished with an olive, is a classic example of a mixed drink.

clue.text: An artist wanted to secure a boat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who works in oils or watercolours

definitions.note: a description of the thing (a rope), not a noun phrase
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the rope at a small boat's bow, used for tying it up

explanation.surface: An artist needed to buy or moor a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted' means needed, describing what the rope is for.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a person who makes pictures and a mooring line attached to a dinghy's bow.

clue.text: The lowest class may well find the boards accommodating always

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one word houses the other

parts.note: treading the boards means acting on stage
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Lowly actors finding a place on the stage forever.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests social class in the theatre; the definition is the cheapest passenger accommodation on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: On old ocean liners, the cheapest passenger quarters were near the rudder gear, the lowest travelling class.

clue.text: A tale that results in a member getting a tip

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body
the tip is the end of something

explanation.surface: A story about a club member receiving a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional story handed down, often historically unverified, is a myth or saga.
